To get started, use the CreateComputeEnvironment or UpdateComputeEnvironment APIs to set accessEntry.desiredState to ENABLED on all AWS Batch compute environments targeting your cluster. AWS Batch creates one access entry per cluster and associates the AWSBatchClusterPolicy with it. You can configure access entries through the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or AWS Management Console. Access entry authentication for AWS Batch on Amazon EKS is now supported in all AWS Regions where AWS Batch is available. For more information, see Amazon EKS access entry authentication in the AWS Batch User Guide .

title: AWS Brazil automates distribution of non-Brazilian software product licenses to Brazilian customers
text: AWS Brazil now provides an automated distribution workflow through the AWS Brazil 2P Distribution Program. Eligible non-Brazilian independent software vendors (ISVs) grant AWS Brazil the right to distribute their Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) product licenses, and AWS Brazil distributes them to customers in Brazil. AWS Brazil is the seller of record, invoicing Brazilian customers in Brazilian Reais (BRL) with applicable Brazilian taxes. The distribution authorizations, seller disbursements, withholding tax calculation, invoicing, and seller reporting are automated. Eligible ISVs agree to the applicable Brazil 2P distribution terms to grant AWS Brazil the right to distribute SaaS product licenses locally by creating distribution authorizations through AWS Partner Central or public APIs. AWS Brazil, as the seller of record, creates private offers for Brazilian buyers, determines the buyer-facing price, and automatically generates invoices, calculates and withholds taxes, and disburses payments. ISVs track transactions and payment status through the Seller Insights dashboard. Buyers in Brazil see private offers priced in USD and invoiced in BRL by AWS Brazil, using the exchange rate on the invoice date. Buyers can pay by credit card (Visa, Mastercard, American Express) or Pay by Invoice (PBI), add a purchase order number, and access invoices in the AWS Billing Console. To learn more about the AWS Brazil 2P Distribution Program, visit the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide and the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide .

title: AWS Client VPN now supports device posture assessment
text: AWS Client VPN now supports device posture assessment, allowing you to verify that connecting user devices meet your security and compliance requirements before granting network access. This feature integrates with your existing device posture providers, so only trusted, compliant devices can access your AWS resources through Client VPN. Previously, Client VPN authenticated users through certificates, SAML, or Active Directory. With device posture assessment, you can now also integrate CrowdStrike , Jamf , or JumpCloud with Client VPN to automatically evaluate device security signals such as compliance scores, encryption status, and risk level before allowing a connection. You define these requirements using Cedar policies , giving you fine-grained control over which devices can connect. To help you author and validate these policies, Client VPN provides you a Test Policy tool that guides you through creating Cedar policies for your device posture requirements. This feature continuously re-evaluates device compliance during active sessions, and automatically disconnects a session if a device falls out of compliance, such as when risk score or security settings change. You can also use this feature in monitoring-only mode, which logs posture evaluation results without disconnecting sessions, so you can assess the impact of your policies before enforcing them. Device posture assessment works alongside your existing authorization rules to provide defense in depth. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Client VPN is available, at no additional cost. This feature requires AWS VPN Client version 6.2.0 or later. To learn more about Client VPN: Visit the AWS Client VPN product page Download the AWS VPN Client Read the AWS Client VPN administrator guide Read the AWS Client VPN user guide

title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available
text: Today, AWS announces the general availability of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities. Continuum for code vulnerabilities discovers, validates, prioritizes, and remediates code vulnerabilities at machine speed. Continuum for code vulnerabilities builds a context graph from your AWS environment, including resource topology, identity relationships, and network reachability. It knows which resources are part of your application, and which findings carry real business risk. It ingests your existing vulnerability findings, scans your code, and then confirms which findings are exploitable by testing them in an isolated sandbox. The findings are prioritized by business impact. And finally, it provides remediation patches as pull requests directly to developer workflows with exploitability proof and blast radius assessment attached. Continuum for code vulnerabilities picks the right AI model for each task. Continuum starts in Learn mode where it proposes the remediation fixes that you approve. When it builds sufficient trust in its precision, you switch to the Enforce mode and let it act autonomous within the guardrails you set. AWS Continuum works alongside your existing AWS security services, including Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub. For more information about the AWS Regions where AWS Continuum is available, see the AWS Region table. To learn more, see the AWS Continuum product page .

title: AWS Direct Connect announces 100G expansion in Bangalore, India
text: Today, AWS announced the expansion of 100 Gbps dedicated connections at the existing AWS Direct Connect location in the Netmagic DC2 data center near Bangalore, India. You can now establish private, direct network access to all public AWS Regions (except those in China), AWS GovCloud Regions, and AWS Local Zones from this location. The Direct Connect service enables you to establish a private, physical network connection between AWS and your data center, office, or colocation environment. These private connections can provide a more consistent network experience than those made over the public internet. For more information on the over 150 Direct Connect locations worldwide, visit the locations section of the Direct Connect product detail pages . Or, visit our getting started page to learn more about how to purchase and deploy Direct Connect.

title: AWS End User Messaging adds a guided wizard for RCS registration videos
text: Today, AWS End User Messaging adds a wizard that orchestrates the entire video capture for your RCS agent registration. RCS registrations in multiple countries, including the United States, require a screen recording that demonstrates your messaging experience. To record it, you have to send a specific sequence of messages to a test device, and until now you scripted those messages yourself, which easily introduced errors and made a mismatched or incomplete video one of the hardest parts of registering for RCS. The wizard now drives each step of the capture for you, sending the right messages in the right order, so you record a compliant video the first time and get your agent approved sooner. The wizard is on all RCS registration forms that require a video submission. To learn more and get started, see the AWS End User Messaging User Guide.

title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports table optimization, statistics, and crawlers for Apache Iceberg V3
text: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports table optimization, statistics, and crawlers for Apache Iceberg Version 3 (V3) tables. With these new capabilities, you can automatically maintain V3 tables, optimize them for query performance, and discover them in Amazon S3. With table optimization, you can compact V3 tables using binpack, sort, or z-order strategies to improve query performance, and remove expired snapshots and orphan files to reduce storage costs. These optimizations support V3 data types, including variant, geospatial, and nanosecond-precision timestamps. You can also generate number of distinct values (NDV) statistics for V3 tables, which analytics engines use to plan queries efficiently. In addition, you can use Glue crawlers to discover V3 tables stored in Amazon S3 and register them in Glue Data Catalog, making them available to query with any V3-compatible engines. These capabilities are available for Iceberg V3 tables in all AWS Regions where Glue Data Catalog table optimization, statistics, and crawlers are available. To learn more, see Glue Optimization , Glue Statistics , and Glue crawlers in the Glue Developer Guide.

title: AWS HealthOmics introduces resource fallback order for Nextflow workflows
text: Today, AWS HealthOmics introduces the resource fallback directive for tasks in your Nextflow workflows, enabling you to define an ordered list of preferred accelerator types, including an option to fallback to CPU instances. Researchers and bioinformaticians can use this directive to reduce time spent diagnosing and resubmitting runs due to accelerator constraints and keep production workflows running. AWS HealthOmics is a HIPAA-eligible service that helps healthcare and life sciences customers accelerate scientific breakthroughs at scale with fully managed bioinformatics workflows. With resource fallback for Nextflow workflows, you can prioritize your preferred accelerator for your task. When your preferred accelerator is unavailable, HealthOmics automatically moves through your specified alternatives in the fallback without resubmission. Each accelerator profile has a configurable timeout, giving you control over how long HealthOmics searches for that accelerator before moving to the next. Shorter timeouts help you move quickly through the fallback order, while longer timeouts increase the probability of reserving your preferred accelerator. You can also include a CPU profile as a final fallback to increase the likelihood of your task reserving an instance. You can now use resource fallback for Nextflow workflows in all AWS HealthOmics Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London), Israel (Tel Aviv), and Asia Pacific (Seoul, Singapore, Tokyo). To learn more, visit the advanced resource configuration and Nextflow specifics documentation.

title: AWS IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now supports change notifications through Amazon EventBridge
text: AWS IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now delivers real-time events to Amazon EventBridge when users, groups, or group memberships or the identity store itself is created, updated, or deleted. AWS IAM Identity Center Identity Store is a central repository that allows you to manage identities and access across AWS accounts and applications, serving as the identity source for AWS IAM Identity Center. This new capability helps you automatically respond to identity lifecycle events and support your security and compliance processes by detecting changes as they happen. With Identity Store change notifications, you can build automated workflows that respond to identity changes in your organization. For example, security teams can create EventBridge rules that trigger AWS Lambda functions to audit user provisioning activity, send alerts to security information and event management (SIEM) systems, or update access in downstream applications when users or groups change. Organizations that manage large workforces can also use this data to automate onboarding and offboarding when users are added to or removed from specific groups. Change notifications are available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available, and events are sent in each enabled Region of your instance. For the list of Regions, see AWS capabilities by Regions . Change notifications are available at no additional cost beyond standard Amazon EventBridge usage charges. To learn more, see Event notifications in the AWS IAM Identity Center User Guide and Identity Store events in the Amazon EventBridge Events Reference.

title: AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Go is now generally available
text: Today, AWS announces the general availability of the AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Go, enabling Go developers to build resilient, long-running workflows using Lambda durable functions. With this SDK, developers can create multi-step applications like infrastructure automation, deployment rollouts with approval gates, and pipelines that call AI models and pause for human review directly in their Go code without implementing custom progress tracking. Lambda durable functions extend Lambda's event-driven programming model with operations that checkpoint progress automatically and pause execution for up to an year when waiting on external events. The AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Go provides a native Go experience for building with Lambda durable functions. It includes steps for progress tracking, callback integration for human and agent-in-the-loop workflows, durable invocation for reliable function chaining, and waits for efficient suspension. The SDK works with the Go tools developers already use. Developers add it to a Go module with go get and deploy their function as a single static binary on the provided.al2023 runtime, like any other Go function on Lambda. Before deploying, they can locally test complete workflows on their own machine with the durabletest package, without requiring network access or AWS credentials, and use the durablelint analyzer to catch code that could break a workflow when it resumes. To get started, see the Lambda durable functions developer guide and the AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Go on GitHub . For Regional availability and pricing details for Lambda durable functions, see the AWS Capabilities by Region page and AWS Lambda Pricing .

title: AWS License Manager now supports license type conversions for Ubuntu Pro purchased through AWS Marketplace
text: AWS License Manager now supports in-place upgrades for EC2 Ubuntu LTS (Long Term Support) instances to Ubuntu Pro available on AWS Marketplace. This allows customers to strengthen their security posture and meet compliance requirements without rebuilding their fleet or migrating workloads to a new instance or AMI. With an Ubuntu Pro subscription, customers receive security patches for up to 10 years — extendable to 15 years with the Legacy add-on. This coverage extends beyond the base OS to thousands of additional packages, including widely used open-source applications such as NGINX, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Redis. Ubuntu Pro also supports Kernel Livepatch, which applies critical kernel security fixes without rebooting to minimize downtime. With this launch, customers, who have an existing Canonical Ubuntu Pro subscription through AWS Marketplace, can upgrade directly during the conversion workflow. Customers who do not yet have a subscription can subscribe to Canonical Ubuntu Pro from within the AWS License Manager console. The new feature is available in all commercial regions where AWS License Manager is available. To get started, navigate to the AWS License Manager console and the AWS License Manager User Guide .

title: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks now supported in the AWS Mexico (Central) Region
text: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks are now supported in the AWS Mexico (Central) Region. Outposts racks extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to virtually any on-premises data center or colocation space for a truly consistent hybrid experience. Organizations of every size, from startups to enterprises to public sector agencies, can now order Outposts racks connected to this newly supported Region to optimize for latency and data residency needs. This regional expansion provides additional flexibility in the number of AWS Regions that customers’ Outposts can connect to. To learn more about second-generation Outposts racks, read the blog post and the user guide . For the latest list of countries and territories and the AWS Regions where second-generation Outposts racks are supported, see the Outposts rack FAQs page .

title: Improve your secrets security posture with actionable recommendations in the AWS Secrets Manager console
text: ​​​AWS Secrets Manager now integrates with the AWS Recommended Actions framework to surface contextual, actionable suggestions for your secrets directly in the Secrets Manager console. ​​ ​​With this launch, you can view tailored recommendations alongside your secrets to improve your security posture and follow best practices without leaving the console. For example, you can identify secrets that need rotation configured, use a customer managed key instead of default service-provided key for encryption, and act on secrets configuration improvements, all from a single view.​ ​​This feature is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where AWS Secrets Manager is offered, at no additional cost. To get started, visit the AWS Secrets Manager console .​

title: AWS Service Reference Information now supports global condition keys, service names, and data plane classification
text: AWS is expanding programmatic service reference information to help you automate IAM policy management and keep your policies aligned with the latest service updates. The service reference now includes all aws:-prefixed global condition keys in a single machine-readable file, a ServiceName field mapping service identifiers to human-readable names, and an IsDataPlane property identifying which actions are data plane operations. You can automate retrieval of this information to eliminate manual effort, and incorporate it directly into your existing policy management tools and processes. This feature is available at no additional cost. To get started, refer to the documentation on programmatic service reference information .

title: AWS Transform for full-stack Windows modernization now supports Aurora PostgreSQL cross-region deployment in 7 more Regions
text: Today, AWS Transform for full-stack Windows modernization adds support for cross-region deployment of converted Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL databases and is available in seven additional AWS Regions. Together these changes give customers more control over where their modernized databases are deployed after SQL Server modernization, supporting data residency, latency, and disaster recovery requirements. Customers can upload SQL Server Database Design Language (DDL) files and set a target AWS Region in the transformation plan to convert the database and deploy the resulting Aurora PostgreSQL cluster to a different AWS Region. The same workflow makes dependent .NET applications PostgreSQL compatible, updating connection strings and ADO.NET and Entity Framework data-access calls. With this expansion, AWS Transform for full-stack Windows modernization is now available in the following Regions: US East (N. Virginia), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Canada (Montreal). To get started, you can go to AWS Transform product page or see AWS Transform for full-stack Windows documentation .

title: AWS Transform for migrations is now available in Asia Pacific (Singapore)
text: AWS Transform for migrations is now available in the Asia Pacific (Singapore) Region, giving customers data residency within the region and lower latency to local source infrastructure as they migrate. AWS Transform is a collaborative enterprise IT transformation service powered by agentic AI that accelerates cloud migration, application modernization, and continuous tech debt reduction. With AWS Transform for migrations, enterprise IT teams can automate the entire migration lifecycle, from discovery and wave planning through network conversion and launching test and cutover instances, using purpose-built AI agents. The service supports infrastructure migration for workloads from virtually any source, including VMware, Hyper-V, KVM, bare metal, and hybrid environments, unifying teams, tools, and workflows in a single collaborative workbench. To get started, see the AWS Transform documentation or visit the AWS Transform product page .

title: AWS Capabilities by Region now offers availability notifications for individual features and advanced filters
text: Today, AWS announces feature-level availability notifications and advanced filters for AWS Capabilities by Region in AWS Builder Center. You can now set availability notifications for AWS service, or to an individual feature of an AWS service, in the AWS Regions you are interested in, and receive an in-app notification and a weekly email digest covering all the capabilities that became available since you enabled availability notifications. Setting availability notifications for a service covers every feature within it, and an 'All regions' option covers every Region, including AWS Regions that launch in the future. In addition to the feature level availability notifications , you can now filter API operations and CloudFormation resources by availability status and compare Regions to show all capabilities, only matching ones, or only differences. With over 19,000 API operations and more than 5,000 CloudFormation resource types, these filters quickly narrow a full listing down to the exact differences between Regions, working alongside search and existing display preferences. Comparing capabilities in AWS Capabilities by Region requires no account. Setting up availability notifications requires a Builder ID, which is free. To get started, visit AWS Capabilities by Region on AWS Builder Center. To learn more, explore the AWS Builder Center FAQ

title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock now supports domain filtering and user location controls
text: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock now supports two new controls that give you more precision over the results that ground a model's response: domain filtering and user location. Both are configured directly on the web_search tool in your existing OpenAI Responses API request. With domain filtering, you can restrict Web Search results to a set of domains you choose. Using the filters parameter, you specify up to 100 allowed_domains to limit results to trusted sources, or up to 100 blocked_domains to exclude sources you don't want. This is useful when you want responses grounded only in specific sites, or when you need to keep certain domains out of results. With user location, you can optionally specify location parameters so that Web Search can return results relevant to that geography. This helps with location-dependent questions, such as regional availability or local services. Domain filtering and user location are available in all AWS Regions where Web Search is supported: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). To get started, see the Web Search section in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide . For pricing, see the Amazon Bedrock pricing page .

title: Bring deep SageMaker AI expertise to your coding agent with the AWS AI/ML skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS
text: Your coding agent can select, train, optimize and deploy models on Amazon SageMaker AI while working across the rest of your AWS environment in a single natural-language workflow. The AWS AI/ML skill is now a core skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS , so it works alongside the toolkit's other AWS skills like EC2, Bedrock, and more. We released the new AWS AI/ML skill on the Agent Toolkit for AWS. The toolkit is now the single, supported integration point, replacing the previous AWS Labs skills and plugins, with a consistent and easy install and update path. The skill is also pre-installed into SageMaker Studio JupyterLab for use with Kiro or your coding agent of choice. Moreover, we extended the SageMaker AI capability areas supported by skills. Inference optimization : optimize deployed models for latency, throughput, and cost Model customization : end-to-end guided fine-tuning workflows, from use case definition through training, evaluation and deployment Serverful training for both traditional ML and generative AI MLflow: experiment tracking and model lifecycle management JumpStart model deployment and model recommendations: deploy pre-built JumpStart models and get guided recommendations on the right model for the use case Processing jobs: data preparation and ETL on managed compute The AWS AI/ML skill is available at no additional charge; you pay only for the AWS resources your agents use. To get started, install the skill from the Agent Toolkit for AWS on GitHub, or use it pre-installed in SageMaker Studio JupyterLab. To learn more about using a coding assistant with your SageMaker AI workflows , see the Amazon SageMaker AI documentation.

title: Amazon Bedrock now offers Canada cross-Region inference for Claude Haiku 5.5
text: Amazon Bedrock now offers Canada cross-Region inference (CRIS) for Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5. Customers with strict data residency requirements can now keep inference processing entirely within Canada. Canada CRIS routes requests only between ca-central-1 (Canada Central) and ca-west-1 (Canada West, Calgary). This helps organizations in financial services, healthcare, the public sector, and other regulated industries meet federal and provincial data residency requirements. Canada CRIS adds to the inference options already available to customers in Canada. US CRIS and global CRIS remain fully supported for Claude Haiku 5.5. Both route requests across a broader set of AWS Regions, and global CRIS also offers cost savings, which makes these options a good fit for workloads that don't require inference processing to stay in Canada. Canada CRIS is designated as an inference profile with limited model selection. Future models and model versions might not be released for this profile. We recommend Canada CRIS for workloads that must keep inference processing within Canada. For more details, see Inference profiles with limited model selection in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. For the most current information about model availability in each Region, see Regional availability by models in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. To get started with Claude models on Amazon Bedrock, visit the Amazon Bedrock console.

title: Amazon CloudFront announces dual-stack support for VPC origins
text: Amazon CloudFront now supports end-to-end IPv6 delivery to origins inside your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC), with the new dual-stack VPC origins. With VPC origins, customers keep their Application Load Balancers (ALB), Network Load Balancers (NLB), and EC2 instances in private subnets that only their CloudFront distributions can reach. With dual-stack support, customers can now send IPv6 traffic all the way to these private origins to meet their IPv6 architecture and regulatory requirements, without exposing origins to the internet. Previously, CloudFront supported dual-stack for public origins but connected to VPC origins over IPv4 only. Customers faced a tradeoff: move origins to public subnets for IPv6 and give up VPC origin security or keep them private and stay on IPv4. Now, with this launch, customers can configure their VPC origins as dual-stack and get end-to-end IPv6 without sacrificing security. Dual-stack VPC origins are available in all AWS Commercial Regions where VPC origins are supported. The full list of supported Regions is available here . There is no additional cost for using dual-stack VPC origins. To learn more, visit CloudFront VPC origins.

title: Amazon Connect Customer supports inline attachment previews
text: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents preview attachments directly in the agent workspace, reducing contact handling time and limiting the need to download sensitive customer information. Agents can preview PDFs, images, and text files across email, chat, and cases, navigate between attachments, and view multi-page documents without leaving the conversation. Amazon Connect Customer attachment previews is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London) regions . To learn more and get started, please refer to the help documentation or visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports customizing the Customer Profiles app on the agent workspace
text: Amazon Connect Customer Profiles now allows administrators to customize which customer data that agents see in the agent workspace, and how it is displayed, using layouts they build in Profile Explorer. Customer Profiles provides agents with a real-time, unified view of each customer during interactions, combining contact history with customer data from multiple sources. Agents who handle different kinds of requests need different customer data in front of them. Within Profile Explorer, administrators can create and save each layout of Customer Profiles widgets, such as contact history, contact information, and lifetime value calculated attributes, and assign it to agents in place of the legacy Customer Profiles view. For example, an airline baggage claims agent sees contact history, active flights, and baggage ticket information, while a loyalty agent sees loyalty status, preferences, and upcoming flights. Layouts can also include an AI Profile Summary that focuses the agent's attention on key customer insights by summarizing the customer profile. You can use Profile Explorer in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more about Profile Explorer, see Profile Explorer in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.

title: Amazon Connect Customer expands testing and simulation to validate flow action outcomes
text: Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to validate the outcomes of your customer experience flow actions during testing and simulation. In addition to confirming that an action started, you can now verify the data it returns when it completes, such as a Lambda function response, an Amazon Lex resolved intent, or the variables set by an Agentic CX block. When a test fails, you can pinpoint the exact action that returned an unexpected result instead of tracing it back from a downstream step, so you can resolve issues faster and launch flow changes with greater confidence. To learn more about this feature, see testing and simulation in the Connect Customer administrator guide. For a complete list of testing and simulation capabilities available by AWS Region, refer to Availability of Connect Customer features by Region . To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website .

title: AWS Lambda durable functions are now available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
text: AWS Lambda durable functions are now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) and AWS GovCloud (US-East) Regions. Lambda durable functions enable developers to build reliable multi-step applications and AI workflows within the Lambda developer experience. Lambda durable functions extend the Lambda programming model with new primitives in your event handler, such as "step" and "wait", allowing you to checkpoint progress, automatically recover from failures, and pause executions without incurring compute charges for on-demand functions. With availability in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, government customers and regulated industries can orchestrate complex processes such as order workflows, user onboarding, and AI-assisted tasks while meeting stringent compliance and security requirements. You can activate durable functions for new Python (versions 3.13 and 3.14), Node.js (versions 22 and 24), Go (versions 1.24 or later), .Net (version 2.2), or Java (17+) based Lambda functions using the AWS Lambda API, AWS Management Console, or AWS SDK. You can also use infrastructure as code tools such as AWS CloudFormation, AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM), and the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). For more information on durable functions, visit the AWS Lambda durable functions product page or the AWS Lambda Developer Guide . To learn about pricing, visit AWS Lambda pricing . For region availability, visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page .

title: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now supports Launch Before Terminate at account-level to replace instances
text: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now lets you enable Launch Before Terminate as the default replacement behavior across all Auto Scaling groups in your account. When enabled, Auto Scaling launches a replacement instance and waits for it to pass health checks before terminating the instance it replaces, helping your applications maintain full capacity and availability during instance replacement events. This applies to replacement events such as instance refreshes, rebalancing, health checks, and maximum-instance-lifetime replacements. You can enable Launch Before Terminate through AWS EC2 Auto Scaling account settings, which let you configure the behavior once at the account level instead of on each Auto Scaling group individually. You can manage the setting with the new `PutAccountSetting` and `DescribeAccountSettings` APIs, available through the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. Launch Before Terminate is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost. To learn more, see Launch Before Terminate in the AWS EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide and AWS EC2 Auto Scaling API Reference Guide .

title: EC2 Image Builder now integrates with ASG for faster image builds
text: EC2 Image Builder now supports using existing instances from an Auto Scaling Group (ASG) for building images, enabling faster builds by eliminating the time spent in launching and bootstrapping new instances and reusing already running EC2 instances. With this feature, you can provide an ASG in your Image Builder infrastructure configuration. Instead of launching a new instance at the build time, Image Builder selects an already-running instance from this ASG, applies your build components, and creates the image. The ASG continuously replenishes the pool as instances are used for builds, ensuring instances are always available for subsequent pipeline runs. This feature is fully opt-in and does not affect existing pipelines. Pipelines without an ASG configured continue to use the default launch path with no behavior change. This feature is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost. To configure ASG integration in your Image Builder pipelines, see the EC2 Image Builder documentation .

title: Amazon ECS Managed Instances adds cross-instance and Spot consolidation
text: Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Managed Instances introduces two infrastructure optimization updates: cross-instance and Spot consolidation. Cross-instance consolidation evaluates tasks running across multiple underutilized instances together, packing them onto fewer instances to raise utilization and lower costs. Spot consolidation extends this capability to Spot capacity, consolidating underutilized Spot Instances after first verifying replacement capacity is available. Amazon ECS Managed Instances provisions, configures, and operates right-sized Amazon EC2 instances for your workloads, balancing availability and cost. Its infrastructure optimization continuously monitors your fleet, reclaiming idle capacity and consolidating underutilized instances with graceful start-before-stop task replacement. Until now, optimization evaluated each instance in isolation for replacement, which worked well when a capacity provider was configured with diverse instance types. However, when a capacity provider was configured with a narrow range of instance types, there were fewer opportunities to consolidate multiple underutilized instances, because no single replacement could yield savings. With cross-instance consolidation, ECS now evaluates and repacks tasks across multiple instances simultaneously. For example, in our testing with a capacity provider configured for c9g instances with a minimum size of 4xlarge, running 261 tasks (each 1 vCPU, 1.94 GiB), cross-instance consolidation reduced the fleet from 19 instances (seven 4xlarge, seven 8xlarge, four 12xlarge, and one 24xlarge) to 13 instances (eight 4xlarge and five 8xlarge), while raising CPU utilization from 42% to 91% and memory utilization from 41% to 88%. Spot consolidation applies the same approach to Spot capacity, first verifying replacement capacity is available. With these enhancements, ECS Managed Instances delivers deeper cost optimization for both your On-Demand and Spot workloads. Cross-instance and Spot consolidation are now available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions, and apply automatically to all existing and new ECS Managed Instances capacity providers. To learn more, see our documentation .

title: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now supports changing durability on existing clusters
text: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now lets you enable or disable durability on your existing node-based clusters. Previously, you couldn't change the durability configuration of an existing cluster in place. This made it harder to move from caching to persistent data store use cases, or to adapt as your application requirements change. Now you can change durability at any point in your application's lifecycle. You can choose between two durability options: synchronous and asynchronous writes. Synchronous writes persist data across at least two AZs before responding to the client, designed for zero data loss at single-digit millisecond write latency. Asynchronous writes persist data after responding to the client, maintaining microsecond write latency at no additional cost. However, up to 10 seconds of uncommitted data could be lost in the rare event of a failure. Both options maintain microsecond read latency. You can now use ElastiCache for a broader set of use cases beyond caching where data loss is unacceptable such as AI agent long-term memory, AI agent workflow state, knowledge bases for RAG applications, payment tokenization, and real-time inventory management. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where ElastiCache for Valkey 9.0 and later is available. To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS SDK, or AWS CLI. For pricing, see the Amazon ElastiCache pricing page . To learn more, see Durability in the ElastiCache documentation.

title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports OAuth for Apache Iceberg REST Catalog APIs
text: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports OAuth 2.0 bearer token authentication for Apache Iceberg REST Catalog (IRC) APIs using AWS Sign-In. The Apache Iceberg REST Catalog specification defines OAuth 2.0 as its standard authentication mechanism, and query engines such as Apache Spark, Trino, and Apache Flink implement it natively. These engines and external integration partners can now authenticate to the Glue Data Catalog Iceberg endpoint using standard OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens, in addition to AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4). You can now grant partners federated access to your Iceberg tables without distributing AWS credentials. Using OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693), you exchange an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity token for a short-lived, Glue-scoped bearer token and include it in IRC requests following the same standards-based pattern used across the Iceberg ecosystem. Access remains governed by AWS IAM and AWS Lake Formation permissions. Common use cases include enabling third-party analytics and data cloud platforms to query tables in the Glue Data Catalog through a single, consistent authentication path. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Glue and Lake Formation are available. To learn more, see the AWS Glue User Guide and AWS Sign-In User Guide .

title: Amazon GuardDuty adds optional threat detection rules for Runtime Monitoring
text: Amazon GuardDuty now supports optional detection rules for Runtime Monitoring. You can enable more than 50 Runtime Monitoring rules that help detect process, file, and network activity that might be routine in one environment but a sign of compromise in another, such as modifying sudoers files or disabling audit logging. The new rules provide detections for Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon EKS, and Amazon ECS on both EC2 and AWS Fargate, and span 13 finding types mapped to MITRE ATT&CK® tactics including persistence, privilege escalation, execution, defense evasion, discovery, exfiltration, and command and control. This release introduces four new finding types: CommandAndControl:Runtime/SuspiciousCommand, CredentialAccess:Runtime/SensitiveFileRead, Discovery:Runtime/SensitiveFileRead, and Exfiltration:Runtime/SuspiciousCommand. To get started, visit the GuardDuty console. You can enable rules in dry-run mode to evaluate detection efficacy before enabling live detection. Custom Detection Rules for Runtime Monitoring is available in all AWS commercial Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, see Amazon GuardDuty Custom Detection Rules . To receive programmatic updates on new Amazon GuardDuty features and threat detections, subscribe to the Amazon GuardDuty SNS topic .

title: AWS Key Management Service now supports ML-KEM for post-quantum key encapsulation
text: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now supports Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM), a post-quantum cryptography standard under NIST FIPS 203 , which enables two parties to establish a shared secret. NIST designed ML-KEM to replace the classical key-establishment schemes, like DH/ECDH key agreement, and RSA-based key transport, in their strategic cryptographic roadmap (see NIST IR 8547 ). ML-KEM addresses the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat to those classical schemes, where an adversary records the key-establishment exchange today and recovers the shared secret once sufficiently powerful quantum computers become available. KMS supports all three ML-KEM key specs defined in NIST FIPS 203: ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024. The Encapsulate API uses the public key to produce a random 32-byte shared secret and its ciphertext form. The Decapsulate API recovers the shared secret from ciphertext using the corresponding private key. KMS protects the private key of an ML-KEM key pair in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated hardware security modules (HSMs). You can use the GetPublicKey API to export the public key and distribute it to partners, client applications, or external systems for performing the encapsulate operation locally using cryptographic libraries like AWS-LC, OpenSSL, or Bouncy Castle. ML-KEM is available in all AWS Regions where KMS is available, except the the Middle East (UAE), Middle East (Bahrain), and China Regions. For more information, see ML-KEM keys in AWS KMS and Key spec reference in the AWS KMS Developer Guide.

title: AWS Lambda recursive loop detection now supports Amazon EventBridge Custom event buses
text: AWS Lambda recursive loop detection now automatically detects and stops recursive loops between Lambda Event Functions and Amazon EventBridge Custom event buses , helping protect you against unintended usage and unexpected charges from runaway workloads. Lambda recursive loop detection , enabled by default on your AWS account, automatically identifies when a Lambda Event Function is invoked recursively by a supported AWS service and stops the loop. You can use EventBridge Custom event buses to invoke Lambda Event Functions, building automation workflows and scheduling recurring tasks without managing any infrastructure. However, a misconfiguration or code defect can cause EventBridge rules to trigger your Event Functions recursively, resulting in runaway usage. Now, recursive loop detection supports EventBridge Custom buses, automatically stopping such loops and sending you an AWS Health Dashboard notification with troubleshooting instructions. EventBridge Custom event buses now support recursive loop detection in every commercial AWS Region where they are available. This feature is enabled by default on your account and requires no configuration. If your Event Function uses recursive loops intentionally, you can use the PutFunctionRecursionConfig API to turn off recursive loop detection for that function. To learn more about recursive loop detection, visit Lambda documentation .

title: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports endpoint connection management
text: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports managing connections through a new endpoint registry, which allows you to register devices or software external to MediaConnect and connect those endpoints to your router inputs and outputs. You can share registered endpoints directly with other AWS accounts, eliminating the need to manually chain router inputs and outputs or coordinate IP addresses and encryption settings out of band. Cross-account endpoint sharing lowers costs by reducing required compute instances and decreases latency through fewer network hops. Sharing is managed through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM), with Connection Manager providing visibility and control over each shared connection. Common use cases include content distributors sharing live feeds with downstream partners, broadcasters collaborating across organizational boundaries, and media workflows that require secure cross-account video transport. MediaConnect endpoint registry is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router is available, at no additional cost. For more information, see the AWS Elemental MediaConnect User Guide .

title: Amazon Neptune now supports online index rebuild to reclaim storage
text: Amazon Neptune Database now supports online index rebuild, a new capability that helps database administrators and application teams defragment Neptune indexes and reclaim unused storage space without taking their database offline. Over time, insert, update, and delete operations create gaps of unused space within data pages, keeping the VolumeBytesUsed metric artificially elevated even after data is deleted. This fragmentation increases I/O costs and degrades query performance for teams running Gremlin, openCypher, or SPARQL workloads at scale. With online index rebuild, read and write queries continue uninterrupted on both the writer instance and read replicas throughout the entire rebuild process. You can target all indexes, only quad indexes, or only dictionary indexes, making this feature well-suited for post-deletion cleanup, periodic maintenance, storage limit management, and performance tuning on heavily fragmented databases. Tunable concurrency and write buffer size settings let you balance rebuild speed against workload impact, while built-in storage safety mechanisms protect against storage exhaustion during the operation. Online index rebuild is available starting with Amazon Neptune engine release 1.5.0.0 on provisioned writer instances, in all regions where Amazon Neptune Database is supported. To learn more about configuring and running online index rebuild, including API references and tuning guidance, visit the Amazon Neptune documentation .

title: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock
text: Today, AWS announces the general availability of OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra on Amazon Bedrock. GPT-6.1 Terra expands the GPT-6 family with a balance of capability, speed, and cost efficiency for everyday workloads. As the newest model in the Terra line, GPT-6.1 Terra combines detailed visual reasoning, accurate computer use, and improved factuality and natural writing over GPT-5.6 Terra, for complex workflows. In OpenAI’s Agents’ Last Exam evaluation, it scored 15 percentage points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra, performed on par with GPT-6 Astra, and completed tasks more than three times faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. GPT-6.1 Terra offers balanced performance with input and output token prices at least 50% lower than those of GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra. It supports a context window of up to 1 million input tokens and accepts both text and image inputs. The Amazon Bedrock inference engine delivers the performance, security, and scale required for enterprise workloads. You can call GPT-6.1 Terra directly through Amazon Bedrock APIs or configure ChatGPT Work and Codex to use the model on Amazon Bedrock. Use it to draft proposals, interpret technical drawings, investigate codebases, and build agents that operate across business systems. Established AWS controls help you secure workloads, govern access, and audit model invocation activity. You can get started in the Amazon Bedrock console or programmatically through supported Amazon Bedrock APIs. For information about supported AWS Regions, endpoints, APIs, features, inference profiles and pricing, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation.

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service introduces validation advisory for domain configuration changes
text: Amazon OpenSearch Service now provides validation advisory for domain configuration changes, which helps you make informed decisions about changes that carry risk but can still be applied. Each configuration validation is now classified as either Critical, which blocks the change, or Warning, which gives advisory guidance that you can acknowledge before you proceed. Previously, validation results were limited to pass or block. There was no way to flag changes that would succeed but carry risk. Validation advisory helps you find potential issues without blocking deployments. Examples include dedicated coordinator nodes that may be too small for the data node configuration, or a shard count that exceeds the recommended limit for the cluster. You can acknowledge warnings when you first submit a change, review severity in dry-run results before applying changes, set acknowledgments directly in AWS CloudFormation templates, and see severity in API responses and Amazon EventBridge notifications. Validation advisory supports all Amazon OpenSearch Service domains running either OpenSearch or Elasticsearch versions. It is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon OpenSearch Service is available. To learn more, see the documentation .

title: Polly Generative engine upgraded with more natural speech, 14 new voices, and 2 new languages
text: Today, we are introducing a new model behind the Amazon Polly Generative engine that delivers more natural-sounding, accurate speech output with low latency. With this upgrade, you get access to an enhanced voice portfolio with higher overall quality, 14 new voices across nine locales, and two new languages—Hindi and Finnish—now generally available on the Generative engine for the first time. New voices include Kenneth and Nate (US English), Russell and Curtis (Australian English), Kiara and Arjun (Hindi and Indian English), Tina (German), Carlos (US Spanish), Leo and Carolina (Brazilian Portuguese), Hyunduk (Korean), and Suvi (Finnish). Amazon Polly is a fully managed service that turns text into natural-sounding speech. This drop-in model upgrade makes Generative voices more natural and accurate. Complex content such as numbers, email addresses, and street addresses is designed to sound more reliable, reducing the need to fine-tune speech output. You can continue to use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) tags to control speech output on the Generative engine, just as before. The low-latency streaming API makes it easy to build contact center experiences, chatbots, and large language model (LLM) based agentic voice applications for real-time conversations. The richness and variety of voice options are also well suited for news, media, entertainment, e-learning, and accessibility use cases. This launch also expands the Amazon Polly Generative offering to AWS GovCloud, providing more options for public sector and regulated industries. All new Generative voices are now available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Zurich), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). To hear how Polly voices sound, go to Amazon Polly Features . For more details on the Polly offerings and use, see the Amazon Polly documentation and pricing page .

title: Amazon RDS Proxy now supports SQL Server 2022
text: Amazon RDS Proxy , a fully managed, highly available database proxy for Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) , now supports Amazon RDS for SQL Server instances running major version 2022. Amazon RDS Proxy sits between your application and the database to pool and share established database connections, improving database efficiency and application scalability. For Amazon RDS for SQL Server Multi-AZ databases, RDS Proxy automatically connects to the standby database instance during a failure, preserves application connections, and helps reduce failover times by up to 83%. RDS Proxy supports standard IAM authentication for SQL Server, where your applications authenticate to the proxy using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) and RDS Proxy manages database connections using credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager. You can enable Amazon RDS Proxy for your SQL Server 2022 database in a few steps on the Amazon RDS console, then connect by pointing your application to the RDS Proxy endpoint. To get started, see our documentation .

title: Amazon Redshift adds support for creating and refreshing Apache Iceberg materialized views
text: Amazon Redshift now supports the creation and refresh of Apache Iceberg materialized views. Materialized views pre-compute expensive joins and aggregations once and store the results in an Apache Iceberg table in Amazon S3 or Amazon S3 table buckets, registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Materialized views are created using familiar SQL — CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... USING ICEBERG and the results are instantly queryable by any Iceberg-compatible engine, including Amazon Athena, Apache Spark on Amazon EMR and AWS Glue, and third-party engines such as Trino, or Snowflake. Redshift keeps them current by recomputing only what has changed with manual incremental refresh, and because the results are Iceberg tables in the Glue Data Catalog, they are governed and discovered like any other catalog table. Data teams often build analytics in stages, stitching together different engines to clean and transform raw data before serving it. This adds pipeline orchestration overhead and can introduce semantic differences between engines. Iceberg materialized views deliver value in two ways. First, instead of hundreds of users and teams re-running the same expensive joins and aggregations, and re-scanning source tables on every query, you compute the result once and everyone reads the precomputed table. Second, you can run an end-to-end pipeline using a single engine like Apache Spark and now Amazon Redshift, and every downstream consumer shares the same open result without the overhead of orchestrating multiple engines. Either way, the output is an open Iceberg table that any engine can read without copies or conversion. You can still load these tables into Redshift Managed Storage (RMS) as native RMS materialized views for your most performance-sensitive dashboards. You can create Iceberg Materialized Views in any region where Redshift Serverless and provisioned Graviton instances are supported. To learn more, see Materialized views stored as Apache Iceberg tables in the Amazon Redshift Database Developer Guide, the CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW command reference, and the Materialize once, query anywhere blog post.

title: Amazon ECR now supports replication backfill for existing container images
text: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replication backfill, enabling you to replicate existing images in your private registry to your configured replication registry destinations. Previously, replication only applied to images pushed after the replication configuration was enabled, requiring customers to manually retag images to trigger replication of preexisting images. With replication backfill, you can now replicate your full image catalog to new or existing destinations with a single API call. Replication backfill is useful when expanding to a new AWS Region, validating disaster recovery readiness, updating replication rules, or ensuring complete image catalogs exist across Regions for compliance purposes. You can run up to ten backfill jobs concurrently, monitor progress and per-image results through new APIs, and stop a job at any time without deleting images that have already been replicated. Replication backfill is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon ECR is available. To learn more, refer to the Amazon ECR user guide .

title: Amazon S3 Express One Zone is now available in 4 additional AWS Regions
text: The Amazon S3 Express One Zone storage class is now available in 4 additional AWS Regions: Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), and Africa (Cape Town). Amazon S3 Express One Zone is a high-performance, single-Availability Zone storage class purpose-built to deliver consistent single-digit millisecond data access for your most frequently accessed data and latency-sensitive applications. S3 Express One Zone delivers data access speed up to 10x faster and request costs up to 80% lower than S3 Standard. It enables workloads such as machine learning training, interactive analytics, and key-value caching in AI search engines to achieve fast data access with high durability and availability. With this expansion, S3 Express One Zone is now available in 19 AWS Regions . For pricing details, visit the S3 pricing page . To learn more, visit the product page and documentation .

title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports custom sequence lengths for serverless model customization jobs
text: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces the ability to configure the sequence length used during your serverless model customization job. Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization supports fine-tuning for many open-weight models, including models from popular families including gpt-oss, Gemma, Llama, Nemotron, and Qwen. Previously, each fine-tuning recipe ran at a fixed sequence length that customers could not modify. Customers sometimes need to modify these parameters to achieve better results for their use case. Customers also asked for longer sequence lengths than the static defaults we supported on some models. Now, you can set sequence length parameters as part of the customization job's hyperparameters, anywhere up to the published maximum for your chosen model and technique. You can set the dataset_max_len hyperparameter for SFT and DPO jobs or set max_prompt_length and max_response_length hyperparameters for RFT jobs. This gives you more control to match your training data characteristics, whether you are working with short question-answer pairs or multi-page documents. Published maximums are up to 16K tokens for many models depending on model and technique. Serverless model customization on SageMaker AI is available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). To get started, navigate to the Models page in Amazon SageMaker Studio to launch a customization job, use the SageMaker Python SDK or use our Agent skills with your choice of coding assistant. To learn more, and see the list of models and supported sequence lengths per technique, see the SageMaker AI documentation .

title: AWS Secrets Manager adds managed external secrets support for Databricks and Twilio
text: AWS Secrets Manager now extends its managed external secrets capability to include Databricks and Twilio, enabling you to automatically rotate the credentials that your data pipelines and messaging applications use to call these services. You set up rotation directly from the AWS Management Console or API without writing or maintaining any custom rotation Lambda functions. Long-lived credentials often stay unrotated because rotation is hard to set up and hard to distribute safely to the applications that use the updated credential. With managed external secrets, you can use Secrets Manager to rotate the Databricks personal access tokens that your jobs and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines use. You can also rotate the service principal OAuth client secrets that your automation workflows use. Each replacement personal access token retains the scopes of the token it replaces, so a narrowly scoped token stays narrowly scoped. For Twilio, you can use Secrets Manager to rotate the API keys and Auth Tokens that your applications use to send messages and place calls. For both services, you store the credential in Secrets Manager as a managed external secret and set a rotation schedule. Secrets Manager always returns the current credential, so your applications pick up rotated values automatically, with no code changes required. These integrations join existing managed external secrets support for BigID, Cisco Security Platform, Confluent Cloud, Datadog, GitLab, Jenkins, MongoDB Atlas, Netskope, Paddle, Salesforce, Snowflake, and SonarQube. Databricks and Twilio managed external secrets are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Secrets Manager managed external secrets is supported. To learn more, visit the AWS Secrets Manager managed external secrets documentation .

title: AWS Security Hub now supports resource criticality for prioritization
text: Today, AWS Security Hub adds resource criticality to exposure prioritization, helping central security teams focus on the exposures that threaten their most business-critical resources. You can set criticality with an automation rule, for example marking every compute resource in a specific account as Very High. The rule applies to resources already in your inventory and to new resources as Security Hub discovers them. Security Hub also infers criticality from resource tags and resource names, with no configuration required, and records which source determined the value. Criticality appears as a column on the Resources page for sorting, filtering, and grouping, and on the Impact assessment tab of an exposure finding. Resource criticality is included with Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost and is always on for all customers. Resource criticality is included with Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost and requires no new enablement. To learn more, see AWS Security Hub User Guide and the AWS Security Hub product page . For a list of AWS Regions where Security Hub is available, see the AWS Region table .

title: Apache Iceberg materialized views now support system-managed write protection
text: Today, AWS announces system-managed materialized views for Apache Iceberg. Materialized views let you precompute an expensive query once and reuse the result across engines. Because this result is an open Iceberg table in your data lake, anyone with write access can change it, either through the catalog or by writing to the files in Amazon S3. System-managed materialized views close this gap by only allowing AWS Glue to write the materialized view's data and definition, so the result stays exactly as computed regardless of who has write access to the table or the underlying S3 files . To get started, write the SQL that defines the materialized view and, optionally, a refresh schedule. AWS Glue then computes the results, stores them as a standard Apache Iceberg table in your Amazon S3 Tables bucket, and keeps them current on your schedule. Because the result is an ordinary Iceberg table in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, any Iceberg-compatible engine can read it directly, while the service guarantees no other writer can alter it. You get a governed, always-consistent dataset that you can confidently share. You can still refresh, reschedule, or drop the view whenever you need to. System-managed Apache Iceberg materialized views are available in all regions where Apache Iceberg materialized views are supported. To learn more, see System-managed materialized views in the AWS Glue Developer Guide .

title: Amazon SageMaker AI announces training session APIs for serverless model customization
text: Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization now supports training session APIs, giving customers full control over their post-training algorithm without provisioning or managing GPU infrastructure. Managed techniques, including SFT, DPO, and other reinforcement learning methods, let customers pick a technique and a model and have SageMaker AI run the training. With training session APIs, teams get to write the training loop, whether that's reproducing SFT or DPO on their own terms or implementing a custom loss, a new RL reward signal, a data curriculum, or an algorithm straight from the latest research. Operations such as forward_backward(), optim_step(), and sample() become API calls against a live, stateful session, so customers compose whatever training procedure their technique requires while SageMaker AI handles GPU allocation, model and LoRA loading, distributed execution, fault recovery, checkpoint storage, and security. Customers can call these operations directly from their own Python code to drive reinforcement learning, supervised fine-tuning, or custom training objectives against a live session, with checkpointing and resume built in. Billing is per token processed, so local computation like reward scoring isn't billed as GPU time. SageMaker AI is also releasing the SageMaker training sessions cookbook , a set of ready-to-run SFT and RL recipes customers can use as blueprints for their own training loops. Training session APIs are generally available today in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Asia Pacific (Mumbai). To get started, install the SageMaker Python SDK and clone the cookbook, or launch a notebook in SageMaker Studio and connect a coding agent. To learn more, visit the documentation and the Amazon SageMaker AI webpage.

title: AWS Transfer Family now supports AWS Secrets Manager storage for SFTP server host keys
text: AWS Transfer Family now lets you store SFTP server host keys in AWS Secrets Manager in your own AWS account. This gives you greater control over your server identity and helps simplify server migrations and failover. Previously, Transfer Family stored host keys within the service, so you could not retrieve the associated private key material. With this launch, you can choose Secrets Manager as the storage type when creating a server or importing a host key. You can then retrieve the private key material and reuse the same host key across servers and AWS Regions. For example, you can use it on a standby server for failover or on a replacement server during migration, without requiring clients to trust a new host key. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies let you control who can retrieve the stored keys. You can also migrate existing host keys to Secrets Manager, which may require additional steps; see the AWS Transfer Family User Guide for details. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transfer Family is available. To learn more, see Store SFTP server host keys in AWS Secrets Manager in the AWS Transfer Family User Guide. To get started, go to the AWS Transfer Family console .

title: TwelveLabs Pegasus 1.5 model now available on Amazon Bedrock
text: Amazon Bedrock now supports TwelveLabs Pegasus 1.5, a video-to-text model that generates structured, time-coded metadata from video. Until now, finding a moment in a large video library meant knowing where to look before you could ask about it. Pegasus 1.5 reads an entire video and labels what happens and when, turning footage into data your applications can query. You define what matters to your business, such as editorial segments, speaker changes, sports plays, or brand appearances, and Pegasus 1.5 finds those moments across the video and returns them with timestamps. It analyzes what it sees, hears, and reads on screen in a single pass, with no pre-indexing or ingestion pipeline to build first. Pegasus 1.5 is accessible through the US and Global cross-Region inference profiles. To get started, visit the Amazon Bedrock product page, access the model in the Amazon Bedrock console, or see the Amazon Bedrock documentation for supported Regions, APIs, features, and pricing.

title: Claude Opus 4.6 now available in Amazon Bedrock
text: Starting today, Amazon Bedrock supports Claude Opus 4.6. According to Anthropic, Opus 4.6 is their most intelligent model and the world's best model for coding, enterprise agents, and professional work. Claude Opus 4.6 brings advanced capabilities to Amazon Bedrock customers, including industry-leading performance for agentic tasks, complex coding projects, and enterprise-grade workflows that require deep reasoning and reliability. Claude Opus 4.6 excels across use cases that require sophisticated reasoning and multi-step orchestration. For agentic workflows, it manages complex tasks across dozens of tools with industry-leading reliability, proactively spinning up subagents and working with less oversight. Developers can leverage Opus 4.6’s coding capabilities for long-horizon projects, complex implementations, and large-scale codebases—handling the full lifecycle from requirements gathering to implementation and maintenance. Enterprise teams can use the model to power end-to-end workflows with professional polish, including financial analysis that surfaces insights requiring days of manual compilation, cybersecurity applications that catch subtle attack patterns, and computer use workflows that move data between applications. The model supports both 200K and 1M context tokens (preview), enabling processing of extensive documents and codebases. Claude Opus 4.6 is now available in Amazon Bedrock. For the full list of available regions, refer to the documentation . To learn more and get started with the model in Amazon Bedrock, read the About Amazon blog and visit the Amazon Bedrock console .

title: Amazon Bedrock expands support for Service Quotas
text: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that provides secure, enterprise-grade access to high-performing foundation models from leading AI companies, enabling you to build and scale generative AI applications. Amazon Bedrock customers can now view inference quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint through AWS Service Quotas. This gives customers a familiar, consistent way to track limits for this endpoint, the same way they already do for the bedrock-runtime endpoint and other AWS services, and gives them clear visibility into the limits that apply to their workloads. The bedrock-mantle endpoint supports the OpenAI Responses API, OpenAI Chat Completions API, and the Anthropic Messages API, letting customers run existing OpenAI or Anthropic based applications on Amazon Bedrock with minimal code changes. AWS Service Quotas now exposes per-model input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas for supported models on the endpoint. With this launch, customers gain visibility into how much limits they have on the bedrock-mantle endpoint and can proactively plan for production scale. To get started, open the AWS Service Quotas console, choose Amazon Bedrock, and search for "Bedrock Mantle" to view your current quotas. To request an increase to any of these quotas, follow the standard Amazon Bedrock limit increase process. Service Quotas support for the bedrock-mantle endpoint is available in all AWS Regions where the endpoint is offered: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Tokyo, Sydney, Jakarta), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Milan, Stockholm), and South America (São Paulo). To learn more, see Quotas for Amazon Bedrock .

title: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights adds 25 new query commands and functions
text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights query language now supports 25 new commands and functions that expand your ability to query, transform, correlate, and analyze logs. Customers analyzing logs in CloudWatch Logs Insights often need to perform statistical aggregation, handle null values in time-series data, compare logs across time windows, detect outliers, and enrich events with lookup data. With this launch, CloudWatch Logs Insights adds type conversion and encoding functions (hexToAscii, hexToDec, decToHex), date and time functions (parseDate, formatDate, queryStartTime, queryEndTime, queryTimeRange), string functions (messageSize), JSON inspection functions (jsonArraySize, jsonArrayContains), and a conditional validation function (isNumeric). It also introduces statistical commands (variance, topk, countFrequent), row-sequencing and null-handling commands (autoregress, accum, filldown, fillmissing), sessionization and time-comparison commands (sessionize, logcompare), a data analysis command (outlier), query-composition and join commands (where, appendcols), and a lookup enrichment command (cidrlookup). These commands and functions are available today in all commercial AWS Regions. To learn more, see the Amazon CloudWatch Logs documentation .

title: AWS Transform continuous modernization is now generally available
text: AWS Transform continuous modernization is now generally available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is supported . This capability helps engineering teams analyze and remediate technical debt across source code repositories at scale. Teams can connect GitHub organizations, GitLab groups, and Bitbucket workspaces, run analyses on demand or on a recurring schedule, and prioritize findings across technical debt, security, agentic readiness, modernization readiness, and custom analysis criteria. With today's launch, you can connect source code providers, initiate and schedule analyses, review findings, and create remediations directly from the AWS Transform web application. For findings with an associated remediation, continuous modernization creates branches and opens pull requests or merge requests containing validated code changes for review. Analysis and remediation run in your AWS account using your credentials, while your source code remains under your control. You can also use the AWS Transform Kiro Power, agent plugins, or AWS Transform CLI to work from your IDE or terminal, analyze local repositories, organize repositories using labels, and run analyses locally or remotely using Amazon EC2 or AWS Batch. To get started, open the AWS Transform web application or use the AWS Transform Kiro Power and agent plugins . To learn more, see AWS Transform continuous modernization in the AWS Transform User Guide.

title: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) now supports prepared statements in Logged Batches
text: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) now supports prepared statements within logged batches, so you can combine the atomicity guarantees of logged batches with the performance and efficiency of prepared statements. You can group multiple prepared INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements into a single atomic batch, where either all operations succeed or none of them do, while reducing query parsing overhead for repeated multi-statement writes. Amazon Keyspaces is a scalable, highly available, and managed Apache Cassandra-compatible database service. Because Amazon Keyspaces is serverless, you pay for only the resources that you use, and you can build applications that serve thousands of requests per second with virtually unlimited throughput and storage. Prepared statements let you define the structure of a Cassandra Query Language (CQL) statement once and run it repeatedly with different values, which improves performance and reduces overhead for frequently executed queries. With prepared statement support in logged batches, you can build atomic multi-statement operations that are both consistent and efficient, using the same CQL statements that you already use. Prepared statements in logged batches are available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where Amazon Keyspaces is offered. To learn more, see Logged batches in the Amazon Keyspaces Developer Guide.

title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports M8i and R8i instances with Oracle SE2 License Included
text: Amazon RDS for Oracle now offers M8i and R8i instances with Oracle Database Standard Edition 2 (SE2) with the License Included (LI). M8i and R8i instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors, available only on AWS, delivering the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. The new instances offer up to 15% better price-performance, and 2.5x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation Intel-based instances. With RDS for Oracle SE2 LI, customers don’t have to separately purchase Oracle license and support. Amazon RDS for Oracle SE2 LI offers subscription based pay-per-use pricing inclusive of software license, support, compute resources, and a managed database service. To use RDS for Oracle SE2 LI, customers can create database instances from the AWS Management Console or using the AWS CLI . and specify the LI option. For more details about how you can lower cost and simplify operations of running Oracle databases, refer to the AWS blog Rethink Oracle Standard Edition Two on Amazon RDS for Oracle . Configuration details for available instance types can be found on the Amazon RDS for Oracle Instance Types page. Review the AWS blog Rethink Oracle Standard Edition Two on Amazon RDS for Oracle to explore how you can lower cost and simplify operations by using Amazon RDS Oracle SE2 License Included instances for your Oracle databases. For pricing and AWS Region availability, see Amazon RDS for Oracle Pricing .
